entries.label: Natural course
entries.why: Without added treatment the heart muscle mass of a hypertrophied ventricle changed little in the one trial that had a placebo arm.
entries.caveat: Simpson 2009 placebo arm: LVMI +1.97 ± 6.68 g/m² over 12 months, 12 patients with normal office blood pressure. Small, short, normotensive. The favourable end is held at no regression. Beyond one year the change is held, not extrapolated.

entries.label: Lower blood pressure
entries.why: Lowering blood pressure a little, even from a normal level, reduced left ventricular mass in a randomised trial.
entries.caveat: Simpson 2009 active arm: LVMI −4.68 ± 7.31 g/m² over 12 months with about 9 mmHg lower systolic pressure, 23 patients with normal office blood pressure. The unfavourable end is held at no regression.

entries.label: Losartan-based regimen
entries.why: In hypertensive patients with LVH, a losartan-based regimen regressed left ventricular mass more than an atenolol-based one.
entries.caveat: LIFE echo substudy: LVMI −21.7 ± 21.8 g/m² from baseline to the last study (mean 4.8 years), 457 patients, ECG LVH with hypertension. No placebo arm; the change replaces the natural course. The unfavourable end is held at no regression. Held after 4.8 years.

entries.label: Atenolol-based regimen
entries.why: An atenolol-based regimen also regressed left ventricular mass in hypertensive patients with LVH, a little less than losartan.
entries.caveat: LIFE echo substudy: LVMI −17.7 ± 19.6 g/m² from baseline to the last study (mean 4.8 years), 459 patients. No placebo arm; the change replaces the natural course. The unfavourable end is held at no regression. Held after 4.8 years.

entries.label: Natural course
entries.why: Aortic stenosis narrows steadily when nothing opens the valve.
entries.caveat: Otto 1997 prospective cohort, 123 adults, mean follow-up 2.5 years: valve area −0.12 ± 0.19 cm² per year, peak velocity +0.32 ± 0.34 m/s per year. Cohort average, not a forecast for one valve.

entries.label: Statin
entries.why: Lowering cholesterol with a statin did not slow the narrowing of the valve in randomised trials.
entries.caveat: ASTRONOMER (n=269, 3.5 years): peak gradient +6.3 vs +6.1 mmHg per year, p=0.83. SALTIRE (n=155): jet velocity +0.199 vs +0.203 m/s per year. SEAS (n=1873): no difference in valve replacement. A statin may still be indicated for other reasons; it does not change this valve model.

entries.label: Natural course
entries.why: Without treatment, Alzheimer's disease shrinks the hippocampi and cortex and enlarges the ventricles at the published average rates.
entries.caveat: Rates from a meta-analysis and older cohorts, applied to one healthy adult volunteer's anatomy. See docs/outlook.md for the per-structure approximations.

entries.label: Aerobic exercise
entries.why: Pooled randomised trials find no clear gain in hippocampal volume from aerobic exercise; one trial found a gain, so the gain is shown only as the favourable end.
entries.caveat: Contested. Two meta-analyses of randomised trials find no significant effect on total hippocampal volume: Firth 2018 (14 trials, n=737; only the left hippocampus was significant, driven by less loss) and Balbim 2023 (8 trials, n=554, healthy older adults, SMD 0.10, 95% CI −0.01 to 0.21). Erickson 2011 (n=120, 1 year) found +2.12% and +1.97% (left, right) on exercise vs −1.40% and −1.43% on stretching, a difference of about 3.46 points: this is the favourable end only. ten Brinke 2014 (n=86, MCI, 6 months) found a gain without a figure in the abstract; EXERT 2025 (n=296, MCI, 18 months) found no group difference. So the likely value and the unfavourable end are held at no effect. None of these trials enrolled people with Alzheimer's dementia.

entries.label: Anti-amyloid antibody
entries.why: Anti-amyloid antibodies slow cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease, but pooled trials show more ventricular enlargement, not less brain loss.
entries.caveat: A meta-analysis of randomised trials (Alves 2023) found that antibodies which cause amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) enlarged the ventricles by 2.1 mL more than placebo (38.7% more; 95% CI 1.5 to 2.8), and the amount tracked ARIA frequency (r=0.86). The same paper reports faster hippocampal and whole-brain loss for secretase inhibitors, not for antibodies. Abushakra 2025 relates slower hippocampal atrophy to slower cognitive decline across anti-amyloid trials, but it is not a pooled volume estimate. The ventricle effect is relative to each trial's placebo and has no per-year rate here, so the button does not change the model.
